newsitem.title: ITALY: Ambroveneto sees cash call within year.
newsitem.headline: Ambroveneto sees cash call within year.

text.p: A capital increase planned by Italy's Banco Ambrosiano Veneto will take place within the year and will happen within the framework of a specific industrial plan, Ambroveneto chairman Giovanni Bazoli said.

Bazoli, speaking at a meeting here, said the proposed capital increase had been postponed because market conditions were not favourable, "but now the market has stabilised and the increase will happen without doubt."
Newspapers have reported that savings bank Cariplo is seeking a strategic link-up with Ambroveneto which could involve Ambroveneto acquiring shares in Cariplo.
Reports say Ambroveneto needs to make a capital increase in order to raise enough funds to acquire Cariplo stock.
However Bazoli declined to comment on the possibility of an alliance with Cariplo.
Asked whether it was important for Ambroveneto to find allies, he replied: "Definitely, given that we are making a capital increase, it would be better to present an industrial plan."

He said enlarging for enlargement's sake made no sense. "You need a project which brings out complementary elements, the advantages of certain associations. We think we have elements which justify the interest there is in us."
